name: Fortis Inc.
moat_justification: Regulated franchise monopolies across 10 North American utility subsidiaries (ITC transmission, UNS Energy, Central Hudson, FortisBC, FortisAlberta, Newfoundland Power et al.) give durable, regulator-granted exclusivity and a visible rate-base growth runway ($28.8B 2026-2030 capital plan, ~7% rate-base CAGR guided), but earned returns are capped at regulator-allowed ROEs, so there is no pricing power beyond the allowed return and regulators can and do reset returns downward (FERC's October 2024 MISO base ROE cut at ITC). That is a moderate/narrow moat: durable cash flows, capped economics.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

FX_CONVERTED: reporting currency CAD converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 40-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Fortis Inc. Form 40-F / FY2025 annual report: the Corporation's common shares are listed directly on the TSX and NYSE under the symbol FTS (release header: TSX/NYSE: FTS); there is no depositary or ADS program — the NYSE line is the same common shares.) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Utilities sector — OE/capex DCF fits utilities names poorly; grade confidence low

Total disclosed stock-based compensation expense FY2025 = C$150M (CAD, as filed; the engine FX-converts at period-end rates).); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact
one_liner: High-quality regulated utility, moat 5/10, but owner's earnings are negative in every filed year (capex for rate-base growth runs well ahead of operating cash flow) — no positive normalized OE, so it cannot clear any hurdle on this model; Tier F by construction, confidence low (utility sector-model mismatch).
moat_for: Regulated franchise monopolies — exclusive electric/gas service territories across five Canadian provinces, ten U.S. states and the Caribbean
Visible rate-base growth: $28.8B 2026-2030 capital plan driving ~7% midyear rate-base CAGR ($42.4B 2025 to $57.9B 2030 guided)
Diversification across 10 utilities and multiple regulators — no single rate case decides the company
52 consecutive years of common dividend increases; 4-6% annual dividend growth guided through 2030
Essential-service demand with low cyclicality; earnings grew through rate-base additions in 2025 and H1 2026
moat_against: Returns are capped at regulator-allowed ROEs — no pricing power; FERC's Oct 2024 MISO base ROE decision cut ITC earnings retroactively ($20M hit to 2024)
Regulatory lag: costs of rate-base growth not yet in customer rates already pressure UNS Energy earnings
Heavy leverage (net debt $24.47B per dcf_numbers.json) and rate-sensitive funding costs
Perpetual equity issuance via the dividend reinvestment plan dilutes share count (~+1.7%/yr share CAGR in the engine blend)
Political/regulatory exposure across many jurisdictions plus CAD/USD translation exposure

Total disclosed stock-based compensation expense FY2025 = C$150M (CAD, as filed; the engine FX-converts at period-end rates).
